ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle JKM, bottom side JM is horizontal, and point L is on bottom side JM; a pink dashed altitude KL is drawn from K to L, labeled 4 ft, and there is a right-angle mark at L. Side JK is labeled 8.5 ft, and side KM is labeled 5 ft. Reasoning: Because KL is perpendicular to JM, △JKL and △KLM are both right triangles. By the Pythagorean theorem, JL = sqrt(8.5^2 - 4^2) = sqrt(72.25 - 16) = sqrt(56.25) = 7.5. On the right side, LM = sqrt(5^2 - 4^2) = sqrt(25 - 16) = 3. Therefore bottom side JM = JL + LM = 7.5 + 3 = 10.5. Triangle area = 1/2 × bottom side JM × altitude KL = 1/2 × 10.5 × 4 = 21.

Then use the triangle area formula with base JM and height KL: area = 1/2 * 10.5 * 4 = 21.
